title: Cross-repo contract registry
problem: How should AgentFactory let repos and workstreams change a shared interface (APIs, events, file formats) without breaking each other, when consumers may sit in other repos, including client-owned ones?
constraints: Zero-dependency MVP: Node built-ins and git only
Respect engagement walls: no shared state across clients
Breaking changes route by decision rights
Some consumers are invisible to us

criteria.text: Catches breaking changes before merge, including semantic ones
Low cost to build and run for a small team
Works inside engagement walls and client-owned repos
Short time to a working MVP

evidence.text: Today's registry is one JSON file of consumer names, read by the fact-checker's no_other_consumers claim.
The Evaluator already replays frozen criteria at a pinned commit, with pluggable checkers.
A change that switched a unit from percent to dollars kept an identical output schema and failed 7 example-based cases.
Consumer-driven contract testing (Pact, can-i-deploy) and schema-registry compatibility modes (backward, forward, full) are established patterns.
Client repos accept our commit trailers and lease refs.
